reason: Start URL https://www.academymuseum.org/en/collection now resolves (HTTP 200) but is editorial highlights only — no per-object catalogue. The catalogued, downloadable flat film art lives on the Academy's OWN infrastructure: the AMPAS Margaret Herrick Library Digital Collections at https://digitalcollections.oscars.org (CONTENTdm/OCLC), an oscars.org subdomain — the Academy Museum's parent collection, not an aggregator. The dmwebservices JSON API is fully open (no auth): dmGetCollectionList, dmQuery, dmGetItemInfo, dmGetCompoundObjectInfo, dmGetImageInfo. 34 sub-collections; in-scope flat film art = production STILLS/photographs, lobby cards, posters, glass slides. Verified live: format facet site-wide = 5,745 photograph + 297 lobby card + 66 poster + 2 drawing. Restricting to single-image jp2 records across the 22 in-scope collections = 4,256. IIIF full/full/0/default.jpg returns the true master (api/singleitem/default.jpg DOWNSCALES — not used); masters are in-gate: photographs 700px long edge, lobby cards ~780px, all >=600px longest edge. Probe ran 15 works end-to-end (API + IIIF download + 600px gate + autocrop + webp + R2 upload), all passed.

exhibitions_entry.name: Academy Museum of Motion Pictures
exhibitions_entry.description: The largest museum in the United States devoted to the art and science of movies, opened in 2021 in the renovated 1939 Saban Building (the former May Company department store) on Wilshire Boulevard, with a spherical David Geffen Theater addition by Renzo Piano. Operated by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences (the Oscars), its galleries trace filmmaking craft, history, and the people behind the movies. The Academy's collecting arm, the Margaret Herrick Library, holds one of the world's deepest archives of film-related flat art — production stills, studio portraits, lobby cards, posters, and promotional glass slides from Paramount, RKO, and the personal papers of directors such as Hitchcock, DeMille, Cukor, and Stevens.
exhibitions_entry.description_ko: 영화의 예술과 기술을 다루는 미국 최대 규모의 영화 박물관으로, 2021년 윌셔 대로의 옛 메이 컴퍼니 백화점 건물(1939년 사반 빌딩)을 개조해 문을 열었다. 렌조 피아노가 설계한 구(球) 형태의 데이비드 게펜 극장이 함께 들어섰다. 오스카상을 주관하는 미국 영화예술과학아카데미(AMPAS)가 운영하며, 전시는 영화 제작의 기예와 역사, 그리고 영화를 만든 사람들을 보여준다. 아카데미의 수집 기관인 마거릿 헤릭 도서관은 파라마운트·RKO의 제작 스틸과 스튜디오 인물 사진, 로비 카드, 포스터, 환등 슬라이드, 히치콕·드밀·쿠커·스티븐스 같은 감독들의 자료를 비롯해 세계에서 손꼽히는 영화 평면 아카이브를 소장하고 있다.

notes:
SOURCE/INFRA: digitalcollections.oscars.org = AMPAS Margaret Herrick Library on CONTENTdm (OCLC), the Academy Museum's parent collection. Allowed per rules (museum's own oscars.org infra). dmwebservices JSON is open and stable; ONE quirk handled in the scraper: dmwebservices returns HTTP 200 with a PLAINTEXT body ('Error looking up ...') both for malformed queries and intermittently under load, so dmFetch reads body-as-text, verifies it parses as JSON, and retries with backoff (5 attempts).

SCOPE DECISIONS: (1) Only single-image jp2 records whose CONTENTdm `format` is in {photograph, lobby card, poster, photomechanical print, slides (photographs)}. Excluded: documents (~12,084 — PCA censorship correspondence/memos), sheet music (~3,082), magazine records, casting directories, scrapbooks/papers that are text, and 3D. (2) COMPOUND objects (filetype 'cpd' — most standalone posters, e.g. autographed Oscar posters in coll9, and multi-page scrapbooks) are SKIPPED; the scraper keeps only single jp2 flat art. Site-wide posters are only 66 and mostly compound, so the loss is small. (3) Lobby cards in coll32 ARE single jp2 (kept). (4) Artist/min-4: `creato` (credited photographer) when present; else for studio-named photo collections (Paramount coll18, RKO coll19, DeMille coll14) the production studio is the documented sourced creator (real archival attribution, same pattern as nfaj using publisher/studio). Records with neither a credited photographer NOR a studio fallback are DROPPED on the min-4 guard (guide §2 — never placeholder a MUST field). This is why estimated_inscope_count (4,256 in-scope jp2 available) > est_full_count (~1,890 collectible after attribution filter). dimensions are always '' (the CONTENTdm catalogue does not expose object dimensions in these collections).

B&W GATE: posters/photographs/prints are NEVER colour-gated (guide §1). colorfulness() is copied from scripts/audit/curate-grayscale-prints.mjs but is logging-only — B&W film stills (colorfulness 0.0) are valid and kept.
